- So the grid is two complete horizontal rows (r3, r6) and two complete vertical columns (c2, c6), forming a hash/grid pattern.
- The yellow ring surrounds the c6 cells of r4 and r5 (the ring spans rows 25-37 = the r3-r6 region, and the interior rows 26-36 = r3..r6 at c6). Wait: the ring's interior is rows 26-36, cols 35-36 = c6 of r3, r4, r5, r6. Currently: r3c6=g, r4c6=w, r5c6=g, r6c6=p.
Hmm, wait, actually the ring's interior: the ring's pixels are at rows 25, 28, 34, 37 (1px yellow at cols 34, 37) and c 2px at (25,35-36), (28,35-36), (34,35-36), (37,35-36), (26-27,34), (35-36,34). So the ring's boundary: top edge row 25 (cols 34-37: Y c c Y), bottom edge row 37 (Y c c Y), left edge col 34 (rows 26-27 c, rows 35-36 c... and rows 28-33? Hmm, the left edge should be at rows 26-36, col 34, but the only c 2px nodes are at (26-27,34) and (35-36,34). What about rows 29-33, col 34? Those should be... part of the panel c! Right — the panel is c, so the ring's "fill" is just the panel color. The yellow 1px at (25,34), (25,37), (28,34), (28,37), (34,34), (34,37), (37,34), (37,37) are the ring's corner markers, and the c 2px at (25,35-36) etc. are... hmm, those are also c, same as the panel. So visually the ring is: yellow corner pixels at 8 positions, forming a 4x13 outline? No wait: the yellow pixels are at (25,34), (25,37), (28,34), (28,37), (34,34), (34,37), (37,34), (37,37) — 8 yellow pixels at the corners of two rectangles: rows 25-28 (top box) and rows 34-37 (bottom box), each box at cols 34-37. So two yellow "O" boxes, each 4x4 (25-28, 34-37 × 34-37), drawn with yellow corners + c edges.
Each box surrounds one 2x2 cell: the top box surrounds (26-27, 35-36) = r3c6 (g). The bottom box surrounds (35-36, 35-36) = r6c6 (p).
So the yellow target boxes are on r3c6 and r6c6! Two target cells: r3c6 and r6c6.
Currently r3c6=g, r6c6=p. The yellow blocks are at r0c5 and r7c2.
Hypothesis: the goal is to bring the yellow blocks to the two target boxes (r3c6 and r6c6).
Now, about the arrows: 6 arrows. What do they do?
- Left red arrows (rows 25-28, cols 13-15) and (rows 34-37, cols 13-15): point right, positioned at the left edge of the grid, aligned with rows r3-r4 and r6-r7.
- Right green arrows (rows 25-28, cols 47-49) and (rows 34-37, cols 47-49): point left, at the right edge.
- Top red arrow (rows 16-19, cols 19-21): points down, above c0-c1.
- Top green arrow (rows 16-19, cols 38-40): points down, above c7-c8.
Maybe each arrow shifts a row or column: the left arrow shifts the left half of the grid (c0-c4) rightward (wrapping?), the right arrow shifts the right half (c5-c9) leftward, and the top arrow shifts the top rows (r0-r4?) downward?
Or the arrows rotate quadrants.
Let me probe: click the top-left red arrow (17, 20) and observe the diff.

sections.label: ASSISTANT
sections.content: The yellow ring is actually two 4×4 target boxes surrounding r3c6 and r6c6. The yellow blocks are at r0c5 and r7c2. Hypothesis: move the yellow blocks to the target boxes. Now, let's investigate what the arrows do.
